title: The full audit replays a root's whole history with a full-state checksum at every step, and again for every waiver event
outcome: The exhaustive audit (doctor, projection repair, backup verification) costs an amount linear in a root's deltas and members, not quadratic or worse, and says what it verifies at intermediate heads.
acceptance: The audit replays each root's history at most once per run, however many waiver events the root has, shown by a test that counts replays

The audit verifies one full-state checksum per root generation, at its final head, together with the continuity of the delta chain, and no longer recomputes the checksum of intermediate states; a test shows the audit's checksum bytes for one root are the same order as one final state at 10, 100 and 1000 deltas
The documentation of doctor says what the audit verifies and what it leaves to the delta chain

When the final checksum or the chain does not verify, the audit reports the root as failed and a separate step-by-step replay names the first delta whose recorded checksum does not match; a test corrupts one intermediate and one final checksum and shows both outcomes
engram doctor on a copy of the live Engram store is timed before and after on the same host and the times are recorded

completion.summary: The full audit replays each root generation once and compares the full-state checksum at its last head only; both required-child waiver passes read that replay; a strict replay names the first mismatching head when the last head disagrees. Landed as commit 3263349 on master, pushed, installed as build da026eb0be80. Doctor on a copy of the live store: 84.5 s and 85.1 s before, 15.1 s and 15.6 s with the installed build. Reduced coverage accepted by Greg: a false checksum on an earlier head while the last head agrees, and an earlier delta change that leaves the final state unchanged, are not detected.
